record.title: China’s phased restrictions on northern and eastern Shan border gates
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Selected northern/eastern Shan gates, with timing and commodity exceptions varying; not all of Muse township exempt
record.crossings: Among reported gates: Manhkar/Namtit, Chinshwehaw, Panghseng, Kyinsankyawt and Nawngtawng; later Mong La and selected Kyalgaung goods
record.direction: Trade into Myanmar chiefly documented; general traveller direction unresolved
record.exceptions: Pangkham and Shawba still open on August 28, 2024; later six restricted reopenings reported.
record.enforcement: Local reporting identifies phased gate shutdowns; ISP subsequently documents selective restricted reopenings.
record.consequences: Residents report aid interruption and rising prices.
record.relationship: Grouped policy regime; child gates should not be added as independent closures without preserving parent overlap. Replaces overly broad exclusion of Muse township.
record.status_observation: Mixed status reported February 3, 2025: some gates reopened with restrictions and others still closed; current status not inferred.
record.official_rationale: No official explanation established; conflict and control by armed opposition contextualise closures.
record.uncertainty: Broad regional umbrella, not a continuous total closure. Sources differ in geographic generalisation; precise gate-specific intervals remain incomplete. No official Chinese rationale established.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No single regional interval is justified.
